```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(commonMZ)
library(dplyr)
library(DT)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r fix-dt-core}
#| echo: false
# pkgdown strips jquery.dataTables.min.js from widget deps (jQuery dedup false-positive).
# Inline the DataTables plugin so the DT tables render correctly.
htmltools::includeScript(
  system.file("htmlwidgets/lib/datatables/js/jquery.dataTables.min.js", package = "DT")
)
```

CAMERA's `findAdducts()` function needs a table of adduct and fragment rules: one row per rule, with columns `name`, `nmol`, `charge`, `massdiff`, `oidscore`, `quasi`, and `ips`. `MZ_CAMERA()` builds exactly that table from commonMZ's curated `adducts_fragments` dataset.

The seven columns are defined as follows. `name`, `nmol`, `charge`, and `massdiff` are described in Kuhl et al. (2012); `oidscore`, `quasi`, and `ips` are documented only in the CAMERA source code.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | character | Ion label (e.g. `[M+H]+`). Display only — never read by the algorithm. |
| `nmol` | integer | Molecules per ion (1 = monomer, 2 = dimer). Divides m/z into neutral mass: `(|charge| × m/z − massdiff) / nmol`. |
| `charge` | integer | Signed ion charge. Multiplied by m/z in the mass formula. |
| `massdiff` | numeric (Da) | Mass added by the adduct or lost as a neutral fragment. |
| `oidscore` | integer | Groups rules that share the same adduct formula but differ in `nmol` (e.g. `[M+H]+` and `[2M+H]+`). CAMERA uses it to automatically extend a monomer match to the corresponding dimer/trimer hypotheses. |
| `quasi` | 0 / 1 | **Mandatory ion flag.** If no rule with `quasi = 1` appears in a candidate group, CAMERA discards the whole group. Typically only the primary protonated ion carries `quasi = 1`. |
| `ips` | numeric | **Ion/adduct peak score** (~0.25–1). Confidence weight per rule. When a peak fits multiple competing mass hypotheses, CAMERA sums `ips` within each group and discards the lower-scoring one. Typical values: 1.0 for `[M+H]+`, 0.5 for multiply-charged ions, 0.25 for neutral losses. |

## Building the rules table

`MZ_CAMERA()` accepts three modes: `"pos"` for positive-ion LC-MS, `"neg"` for negative-ion LC-MS, and `"ei"` for electron-ionisation GC-MS. The `warn_clash` argument flags pairs of rules whose mass differences fall within a given ppm tolerance of each other and cannot be distinguished on mass alone.

### Positive mode

```{r rules-pos}
rules_pos <- MZ_CAMERA(mode = "pos", warn_clash = TRUE, clash_ppm = 5)
nrow(rules_pos)
```

Browse the full table — sort any column or use the search box to filter by name or mass difference:

```{r rules-pos-table}
DT::datatable(
  rules_pos %>% mutate(massdiff = round(massdiff, 4)),
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 15, order = list(list(3, "asc")))
)
```

### Negative mode

```{r rules-neg}
rules_neg <- MZ_CAMERA(mode = "neg", warn_clash = TRUE, clash_ppm = 5)
nrow(rules_neg)
```

```{r rules-neg-table}
#| code-fold: true
DT::datatable(
  rules_neg %>% mutate(massdiff = round(massdiff, 4)),
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 15, order = list(list(3, "asc")))
)
```

### Electron ionisation (EI)

```{r rules-ei}
#| code-fold: true
rules_ei <- MZ_CAMERA(mode = "ei", warn_clash = FALSE)
nrow(rules_ei)
```

## The NH₄⁺ clash

A common clash in positive mode: `[M+NH4]+` and neutral loss of NH₃ produce the same 17.027 Da difference and cannot be distinguished on mass alone. The warning from `warn_clash = TRUE` flags this. If NH₄⁺ adducts are rare in your matrix (common for many reversed-phase LC-MS setups), remove them before passing the rules to CAMERA:

```{r remove-nh4}
rules_pos_clean <- rules_pos %>% filter(name != "[M+NH4]+")
nrow(rules_pos_clean)
```

## Complete example: CAMERA's built-in data

The steps below annotate `mm14`, CAMERA's built-in example xcmsSet (134 peaks, single-sample, positive mode), using commonMZ rules. The workflow has five stages:

**Step 1 — create an `xsAnnotate` object** from an xcms result:

```{r step1}
#| eval: false
library(CAMERA)
library(xcms)

# xs is an xcmsSet produced by xcms peak detection
cam_pos <- xsAnnotate(xs, polarity = "positive")
```

**Step 2 — group co-eluting peaks** by retention time window (FWHM-based):

```{r step2}
#| eval: false
cam_pos <- groupFWHM(cam_pos, perfwhm = 0.6, intval = "into")
```

**Step 3 (optional) — refine groups by cross-sample correlation:**

```{r step3}
#| eval: false
cam_pos <- groupCorr(cam_pos, cor_eic_th = 0.7, pval = 1e-6,
                     calcIso = FALSE, calcCiS = FALSE, calcCaS = TRUE)
```

**Step 4 — annotate isotope peaks:**

```{r step4}
#| eval: false
cam_pos <- findIsotopes(cam_pos, ppm = 10, mzabs = 0.01)
```

**Step 5 — annotate adducts and fragments with commonMZ rules.** CAMERA requires a plain `data.frame`, not a tibble, so wrap with `as.data.frame()`:

```{r step5}
#| eval: false
cam_pos <- findAdducts(cam_pos,
                       ppm        = 10,
                       mzabs      = 0.01,
                       multiplier = 3,
                       polarity   = "positive",
                       rules      = as.data.frame(rules_pos_clean))
```

`multiplier` controls the highest oligomer CAMERA will consider (e.g. `[2M+H]+`, `[3M+H]+`). `ppm` and `mzabs` set the matching tolerance; CAMERA applies whichever window is wider, so for high-resolution data keep `mzabs` small (0.005–0.01) and rely on `ppm`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The code below runs this pipeline on `mm14`, the xcmsSet bundled with CAMERA (134 peaks, single-sample, positive mode), to produce the outputs shown here.

```{r run-example}
#| code-fold: true
library(CAMERA)

data("mm14")                                          # xcmsSet from CAMERA package

xsa        <- xsAnnotate(mm14, polarity = "positive")
xsaF       <- groupFWHM(xsa, perfwhm = 0.6, intval = "into")
xsaI       <- findIsotopes(xsaF, ppm = 10, mzabs = 0.01, intval = "into")
cam_result <- findAdducts(xsaI,
                          ppm        = 10,
                          mzabs      = 0.01,
                          multiplier = 3,
                          polarity   = "positive",
                          rules      = as.data.frame(rules_pos_clean))
```

## Annotated peak table

`getPeaklist()` returns one row per feature with annotation columns appended. The `adduct` column shows the best-matching rule for each feature; features with no match are left blank.

```{r peaklist-table}
#| code-fold: true
peaklist <- getPeaklist(cam_result)

DT::datatable(
  peaklist %>%
    select(mz, rt, any_of(c("isotopes", "adduct", "pcgroup")),
           starts_with("sample")) %>%
    mutate(mz = round(mz, 4), rt = round(rt, 1)),
  rownames = FALSE,
  options  = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

## Which rules fired?

After annotation, count how often each rule was assigned. Rules that fired zero times are either absent from this matrix or could not be resolved within the tolerance.

```{r rules-freq}
#| code-fold: true
rules_count <- cam_result@annoID[, "ruleID"] %>%
  factor(levels = seq_len(nrow(rules_pos_clean))) %>%
  table() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  setNames(c("ruleID", "n")) %>%
  mutate(name = rules_pos_clean$name[as.integer(ruleID)]) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

total <- sum(rules_count$n[rules_count$n > 0])
pie_data <- rules_count %>%
  filter(n > 0) %>%
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = name)) %>%
  mutate(
    cumend   = cumsum(n),
    cumstart = cumend - n,
    mid      = (cumstart + cumend) / 2,
    on_right = mid / total < 0.5
  )

set1_no_yellow <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Set1")
set1_no_yellow <- set1_no_yellow[set1_no_yellow != "#FFFF33"]
pie_colors <- rep(set1_no_yellow, length.out = nrow(pie_data))

ggplot(pie_data) +
  geom_col(aes(x = 0.5, y = n, fill = name),
           width = 1, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 1.0, xend = 1.2, y = mid, yend = mid),
               linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  geom_text(aes(x = 1.25, y = mid, label = name,
                hjust = ifelse(on_right, 0, 1)),
            size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(pie_colors, levels(pie_data$name))) +
  coord_radial(theta = "y", start = 0, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void()
```

```{r rules-sankey}
#| code-fold: true
iso_of <- function(x) sub("^.*?\\[M([^\\]]*)\\].*$", "[M\\1]", x, perl = TRUE)

sk_adducts <- peaklist %>%
  filter(trimws(adduct) != "") %>%
  mutate(rule_name = trimws(sub("\\s+[0-9.]+$", "", adduct))) %>%
  left_join(rules_pos_clean %>% select(name, nmol), by = c("rule_name" = "name")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(nmol)) %>%
  mutate(
    mult     = paste0("[", nmol, "M]"),
    iso_type = ifelse(trimws(isotopes) == "", "no isotope annotation", iso_of(isotopes))
  )

# Isotope-only peaks (no adduct): [M+1],[M+2]… satellite peaks → terminal at col 2.
# Exclude [M] iso-only peaks: they have no adduct so cannot flow to nM/adducts,
# and merging them into the [M] node would break flow conservation.
sk_iso_only <- peaklist %>%
  filter(trimws(isotopes) != "", trimws(adduct) == "") %>%
  mutate(iso_type = iso_of(isotopes)) %>%
  filter(iso_type != "[M]")

# Flow: All annotations → iso_type → nM multiplicity → adduct rule
#
# [M+1],[M+2]… are terminal: isotope satellites stop at col 2.
# [M] and "no isotope annotation" (adduct peaks only) flow on to nM → adducts.
#
#   col 1 (x=0.01): All annotations
#   col 2 (x=0.33): no isotope annotation | [M] | [M+1] | [M+2] | …
#   col 3 (x=0.66): [1M] | [2M] | …   (only from [M] and "no isotope annotation")
#   col 4 (x=0.99): adduct rules by frequency

sk_through <- sk_adducts %>% filter(iso_type %in% c("[M]", "no isotope annotation"))

# All Sankey edges in one flat table
iso_all <- bind_rows(sk_adducts["iso_type"], sk_iso_only["iso_type"])

edges <- bind_rows(
  transmute(iso_all,    from = "All annotations", to = iso_type),
  select(sk_through,    from = iso_type,          to = mult),
  select(sk_through,    from = mult,              to = rule_name)
) %>%
  count(from, to, name = "n")

# Node ordering per column
iso_lvl   <- c("no isotope annotation", "[M]", "[M+1]", "[M+2]", "[M+3]", "[M+4]")
iso_nodes <- edges %>%
  filter(from == "All annotations") %>%
  pull(to)

iso_ord   <- c(intersect(iso_lvl, iso_nodes), setdiff(iso_nodes, iso_lvl))

mult_ord <- edges %>%
  filter(from %in% c("[M]", "no isotope annotation")) %>%
  group_by(to) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  pull(to)

rule_ord <- edges %>%
  filter(from %in% mult_ord) %>%
  group_by(to) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  pull(to)

col_nodes <- list("All annotations", iso_ord, mult_ord, rule_ord)
col_x_val <- c(0.01, 0.33, 0.66, 0.99)
all_nodes <- unlist(col_nodes)

links <- edges %>%
  transmute(source = match(from, all_nodes) - 1L,
            target = match(to,   all_nodes) - 1L,
            value  = n)

# Node flow derived from edges: max(in, out) — equal for pass-through nodes,
# whichever is nonzero for source/terminal nodes
node_flow_df <- bind_rows(
    edges %>% group_by(node = from) %>% summarise(n = sum(n)),
    edges %>% group_by(node = to)   %>% summarise(n = sum(n))
  ) %>%
  group_by(node) %>%
  summarise(n = max(n), .groups = "drop")
node_flow <- setNames(node_flow_df$n, node_flow_df$node)

# Compute proportional y-centres for nodes in a column (top=0, bottom=1)
calc_y <- function(nodes, flows, gap = 0.01) {
  f <- pmax(flows[nodes], 1)
  total <- sum(f)
  n <- length(f)
  usable <- 1 - gap * (n - 1)
  h <- f / total * usable
  starts <- cumsum(c(0, h[-n] + gap))
  setNames(pmin(pmax(starts + h / 2, 0.001), 0.999), nodes)
}

node_x <- rep(col_x_val, lengths(col_nodes))
node_y <- unname(unlist(lapply(col_nodes, calc_y, flows = node_flow)))

plotly::plot_ly(
  type = "sankey", arrangement = "fixed",
  height = 800,
  node = list(
    label     = all_nodes,
    x         = node_x,
    y         = node_y,
    pad       = 15,
    thickness = 20
  ),
  link = list(source = links$source, target = links$target, value = links$value)
) %>%
  plotly::layout(margin = list(r = 160)) %>%
  htmlwidgets::onRender(paste(readLines("sankey-label-fix.js"), collapse = "\n"))
```
